logline: A man reading his poem to a lover who keeps his back turned watches him go off the fire escape, follows him down through the world's escapes into a party that will not hold him, and falls out of life.
reading:
The poem opens with a disowning ('What we've made we don't want... doesn't exist') and becomes a search through a home turned maze: hallways, drawers, fire escapes. The love is 'tainted', a 'make-believe haven' over quicksand, an 'overnourished forest of escapism' that calls the EX away. The speaker commits to following anyway: 'I'll follow... to rediscover when love was real.' He admits failure ('I failed at protecting you from your own vices') and crashes 'the party of your evilest instincts'.

The hinge is 'trip on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave' (L02-L03). His own words make him fall, and the title question becomes a place. The poem ends on the same phrase with a new verb, 'landing into the secret', so the fall turns out to be a way of arriving. Governing images: the back turned to him ('With your back faced against me'), the words he trips on, the drop, and 'sweet memories and photographs, film and fiction that leave me empty', which makes the archive footage part of the poem's own material.
motifs: the turned back: EX is only ever a back, at the rail and in the crowd
tripping on his own words: the poem page he holds, letters coming loose
ways out that are not: hallway door, drawer, fire escape
haze: vape cloud that thickens until the window recedes
the fall as following: always one body-length behind, the gap never closing
escape media: TV, phone screens, party lights, pills
film and photographs that leave him empty: the archive as memory that fails
the ember: the one sharp point in the haze and the dark

light_and_texture: Cold practical light: TV glow and city spill through glass. The puppet is lit from the window side so his face card reads against blue. Haze is layered tracing paper and torn vellum on separate rails, not a digital blur, so every layer has an edge. Cards are dark corrugated board with the flutes showing through thin gouache. The vintage party is the exception: POET stays in full colour while the ballroom and its painted dancers are silver-grey, as if he has fallen into an old film.

fx.how: 3-4 sheets of torn tracing paper on horizontal rails at different depths; the plume itself is a tissue card from EX's hand. Foggy Mountain (2007) as a 15% overlay for drift.
slide the tracing-paper rails in from frame left one after another; each layer knocks the window's contrast down.
code: sample the archive clip's luminance and modulate a blue light card on the wall and POET's front edge.
POET card mirrored at 20% opacity on the acetate glass layer, offset for parallax.
scale the window and EX plate down while POET's hand grows; the gap widens as he walks.
long strips of lit-window card (or Communications Primer frames) scroll upward behind the fallers with motion-blur smears painted on the board.
cut-paper letters from the poem page peel off and fall alongside him. 'Trip on my own words', made literal.
archive film burn and bokeh (Moonwalk One / Master Hands) screened over the party in gold.
step-print the dancers (hold every pose 4 frames) while POET moves at normal speed.
the EX card is sliced into strips that drop away one at a time.
parquet card swaps whole → cracked → holed; black behind; POET slides behind the front lip.
black ink bleeding through wet paper, shot flat and keyed as a matte that eats the frame dot by dot.

passage.keep: The hand that stops short reads as a refusal to touch what is leaving. 'You can't leave us out here' (Under Western Stars) answers 'where you go when you leave' from the side of the one left behind. The window is the right surface.
passage.better: Use the figure-free glass wall gen_a63bb494b1 instead of the scene-book plate, which has a generated man in it. Open the archive in ONE tall pane, bright and large, with EX's back card faint in the next pane. Add a fire-escape rail card outside so the geography holds. Swap the head to 'down' on the answer. Fix the fulcrum note: 'where SHE goes' should be 'where he goes'.
alt_lines: L02 'I look for a way out through the hallways': grip on the door frame; Alice In Wonderland (1915) intertitle 'Doors all round and all locked' opens in the hallway doorway.
L13 'and photographs, film and fiction that leave me empty': hand opens and the page drops; Appreciating Our Parents (1950) plays in the CRT screen.
L14 'With your back faced against me, you offer me a new pursuit of happiness': page held out toward EX's back; Beginning to Date (1953) opens in the window pane between them.
L09 'I failed at protecting you from your own vices': hand stops short of EX's shoulder in the crowd; His Royal Highness (1932) dancers fill the ballroom arch behind.

ideas: TV inside TV: the CRT card in gen_2a594d9e83 has its screen cut out, and 1959 RCA 21-inch TV Screen plays in it under the opening line 'what we've sold to the world... doesn't exist'.
Drawers inside drawers: on 'within the drawers' the drawer slides open and Health: Your Posture (1953) fills it, a room full of dressers.
The facing building is the archive: General Health Habits (1928) tenement escapes stand behind EX's back on the landing. A 1928 fire escape opposite a 2025 one.
He trips on his own words: letters peel off the poem page and fall with him past view_038's tower canyon. Escape-screen bezels carry gen_0b067a1c52 and Communications Primer windows.
The forest that calls: gen_366225426b (framed misty forest) floats as a lit window in the void on L05, and EX falls toward it, not away from POET.
Colour into grey: POET lands in full colour inside His Royal Highness (1932). The painted dancers are silver-grey. Under Western Stars couples turn in step-print while EX's back strips away.
Quicksand under the haven: Aluminum on the March (1956) powder pour fills the floor hole as he sinks on 'pit beneath the quicksands'.
Exit through the eye: gen_24ac458d01 iris → gen_9f26db2b7a black pupil ring; push in until the pupil is the black of 02.
